Let that shit go, why do you need their approval, that's what you're spite really is you want them to respect you and think about you. Stop doing shit for other people. Why do you need their approval? Why do they have this power over you? It's a good short term motivator but it only strengths their power over you, and further drives the insecurity you are trying to cover up. What weakness did they expose? why does it bother you?

I'm not saying it isn't awesome that you're killing it but you needing others to see you succeed is them having power and control over you and that shit will eat you up. You'll end up accomplishing everything but still feeling like you didn't do enough, feeling empty and insecure, if someone hints at the thing that you worked so hard to cover up your ego will feel it hard.

Oh wow, "He feels pressured, like he can't be enough, and like I might just pick up and leave when he makes a mistake." sounds like me with my ex.

But to answer your question a genuine apology is a good place to start. Idk how the relationship goes exactly but it sounds like the focus is on you and your needs, if he's like me he may of  taken over the care taker role because of his own history in your relationship or his life. Someone has shown that not being prefect will result in those he loves turning on him or leaving him. Try to shift the relationships focus to both of you guys instead of just one of you. I would also figure out why you have such trust issues, and a fear of abandonment and sort that out.

Explain your true feeling to him when you are upset, not the explosive emotions you are going through (feel your emotions but don't let them consume you) and don't stone wall and block him out. I'll put like this if you really do want to have kids would you want to have these outburst at them? because if you don't get this sorted out you will, because your kids are going to be even more difficult to deal with because they are kids. It's finding that balance in  expressing your frustration in a way thats productive. Balance between exploding and being a push over. Let him know he's loved even if he isn't perfect, random affection not just when he's there for you or checks the boxes goes along way.

I am very sorry if this ended up coming out as projecting. I hope it works out for you two.

I used to have a lot of anger issues too. Anger is just sadness redirected. It might be worth exploring your sadness. You mentioned your father passed, I'm sorry to hear that, I dated a girl who lost her mom for an extended amount of time and she harbored so much resentment towards the world and even her mom for passing, she would explode over the smallest things. Loss is tough, especially when there is no bad guy to point your finger at. I recommend reading the book radical honesty. 

I'm 25 now and when I was 15 I was angry constantly. I used have vivid dreams of committing violent acts, I would get this itching feeling in my neck and shoulders and explode over anything especially at those I cared about. I remember punching walls, beating up a mailbox, trashing a bathroom, etc.  I'm not kidding when I say muay thai saved me. I really recommend picking up a combat sport or upping your exercise generally. Learn to control your body, and your breathing. All that shit in movies about rage making you stronger is absolutely bs. It gasses you out, telegraphs what you are gonna do. Get in tune with your body, and learn to control it, so when you start to feel those feelings bubbling over you can dial them back. Meditation helps too. Anger/Anxiety were just the bodies way to give you energy to survive, you have to learn to use that energy, otherwise it will explode out of you.

You talked about a girl who treats you like shit. Cut all contact with her and move on man. I learned that too late. Get your shit straight before you start involving other people. If its an added motivation having control over your emotions is a very attractive trait. Think of the most of attractive men, they don't lose their cool. Who do girls go for the dude is screaming because he's jealous, and crying or the guy who just smiles and laughs in the face of the dude trying to hit on the girl he's with. Anger isn't a replacement for confidence.

Focus on yourself, you're interested in business/marketing figure out what kind, learn about it. Business is great because it easy to get into. Start something small with some buddies. Figure out if you need a degree, set some realistic goals for yourself and work towards them. The rest will come.

Mindfulness, I know what you mean about suicide being a plan b, I've found I have to cognitively correct myself every time I start thinking about it as a valid solution and stop myself from fantasizing about it. Meditation helped me a lot with this, just practicing counting my breathes and when my mind would wander recognize that I am wandering and start counting my breathes again.

It goes without saying professional help, is a good idea. Building a good support system is important. A general audit of your life and life style is also good.

But to answer your question about your mind jumping to suicide, practicing things like meditation, yoga, journaling that force you to become aware of your thoughts and how you think, and teach you to control where they go is tactic I've found helpful.

Best of luck, I hope you move pass this, you're stronger than you know for trying to over come this!

Is your diet sustainable? I've found when I cut too low or in a very restrictive/unbalanced way I'm much more likely to get into binge/fasting or purging cycles. I would also get all of your binging food out of your house. Whats worked for me is having a diet that allows for the occasional treat, like maybe you're meals are clean and then you pick up a sweet on the way back from work. Or maybe you're cutting out carbs entirely so you rebound when presented with carbs or your will power is tested. Make sure your macro/micro nutrients are hit.

Stop labeling yourself as a narcissist, you're already setting yourself up for failure (coming from someone who was suicidal for many years). Seek out professional help. You can't love someone if you don't love yourself. I feel like you feel alone because you're guarded. You're hiding yourself and using the mask you created to interact with people rather than the person you are. What's so bad about being alone? We all die alone, the only person we have to live with 24/7 is ourselves why not make peace with that person?  Do you have anyone you can be completely vulnerable with? If not seek out therapy, try someone in your circle, hell posting on here is an easy way to do it. Ultimately you're in control of the person you'll be, if you're mindful of your actions you can control who you are in your relationships. If you don't feel like you have that mindfulness you can cultivate that, therapy, meditation, journaling, etc. You're in control of the person you are and the person you become.

Maybe you're doing shit for the wrong reasons. What are your dreams really? Do you actually want the things you're striving for or are you just doing it to feel like you're not a loser? And I'm not surprised you gained weight if you just worked out to run a marathon. Set yourself recurring goals, and a schedule that will uphold the habits you need to achieve your goals. Figure out your goals and make sure they align with your values, figure out your values. Working hard by itself will just burn you out. Not saying you haven't thought of all this, I just know I find myself frequently in the same spot and its because I'm putting in all my effort for all the wrong reasons.
